CREATE TABLE orders (id INT PRIMARY KEY)

typed_oracle.sql_law: CREATE primary key forbids duplicate and NULL keys. A following duplicate INSERT is rejected without changing the unique physical row.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT REFERENCES customers(id))

typed_oracle.sql_law: Foreign key references customers(id); rows referencing present parents survive, and absent parent 99 is rejected without target state mutation.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT UNIQUE)

typed_oracle.sql_law: UNIQUE(id) forbids repeated non-NULL id=1 while allowing two independent NULL rows.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT NOT NULL)

typed_oracle.sql_law: NOT NULL(id) permits positive/negative integers and rejects NULL insertion without altering existing rows.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT CHECK (id > 0))

typed_oracle.sql_law: CHECK(id > 0) rejects FALSE id=0 while SQL UNKNOWN is distinct from failed truth under standard SQL CHECK.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT DEFAULT 1)

typed_oracle.sql_law: DEFAULT 1 supplies omitted id only; an explicit id=2 is retained. Final bag contains distinct 1 and 2.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, amount INT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (id + 1))

typed_oracle.sql_law: GENERATED ALWAYS (id+1) computes amount=2,3 from inserted id 1,2. The computed column is not an independent source assignment.

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT PRIMARY KEY, amount DECIMAL(10,2))

typed_oracle.sql_law: CREATE TABLE declares enforced PK id and DECIMAL(10,2) amount; source insert of 10.25 preserves scale and duplicate id=1 is rejected.

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders

cases.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT PRIMARY KEY, amount DECIMAL(10,2))

cases.sql: SELECT id FROM orders

typed_oracle.sql_law: Original SELECT id FROM orders cannot invent source columns or types when both catalog and manifest omit them. Conflicting warehouse and manifest types follow catalog authority.

cases.sql: INSERT INTO orders (id, amount) VALUES (1, 10)

cases.sql: INSERT INTO orders (id, amount) SELECT id, amount FROM customers

typed_oracle.sql_law: INSERT SELECT copies all three independent customers row occurrences into orders, retaining two duplicate (4,40) tuples and unchanged customers source.

cases.sql: INSERT INTO orders (id, amount) VALUES (1, 10), (2, NULL)

typed_oracle.sql_law: Multi-row INSERT appends exactly (1,10) and (2,NULL), preserving pre-existing duplicate (2,20) rows.

cases.sql: INSERT INTO orders (id, amount) VALUES (1, 10) RETURNING id

typed_oracle.sql_law: INSERT RETURNING emits the inserted id=1 once and appends exactly one target row.

cases.sql: INSERT INTO orders (id) VALUES (1) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING

typed_oracle.sql_law: ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING against an enforced primary key with id=1 already present inserts zero rows; target state stays identical.

cases.sql: REPLACE INTO orders (id) VALUES (1)

typed_oracle.sql_law: MySQL-style REPLACE INTO has engine-specific destructive conflict rules; original DuckDB rejects it, so there is no valid DuckDB poststate or portable Exact claim.

cases.sql: INSERT OVERWRITE TABLE orders SELECT * FROM customers

typed_oracle.sql_law: INSERT OVERWRITE needs storage/partition replacement scope unavailable to the portable analyzer; DuckDB rejects the original syntax. No fabricated successful state.

cases.sql: UPDATE orders AS o SET amount = c.amount FROM customers c WHERE o.id = c.id

typed_oracle.sql_law: UPDATE FROM selects target id=1 only from one matching customers source occurrence. id=NULL is UNKNOWN, duplicate id=2 rows are untouched.

cases.sql: UPDATE orders SET amount = amount + 1 WHERE id > 0

typed_oracle.sql_law: Computed UPDATE amount+1 for id>0 selects four physical rows; NULL amount stays NULL, duplicate id=2 occurrences both become 21; NULL id is UNKNOWN.

cases.sql: UPDATE orders SET amount = 1 WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM customers)

typed_oracle.sql_law: Correlated IN UPDATE selects id=1 under the complete customers bag, with NULL id UNKNOWN; original analyzer reports an unsupported subquery, so native success cannot be promoted to Exact.

cases.sql: UPDATE orders SET amount = 2 WHERE id = 1 RETURNING id

typed_oracle.sql_law: UPDATE RETURNING id=1 updates one target row to amount=2, returns one id=1, and preserves other physical rows.

cases.sql: DELETE FROM orders USING customers WHERE orders.id = customers.id

typed_oracle.sql_law: DELETE USING customers selects target id=1 once. Multiple unmatching customer id=4 occurrences cannot delete an absent target.

cases.sql: DELETE FROM orders WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM customers)

typed_oracle.sql_law: DELETE WHERE id IN (SELECT id ...) selects target id=1 while NULL id is UNKNOWN; original analyzer reports unsupported subquery, not an Exact physical proof.

cases.sql: DELETE FROM orders WHERE amount IS NULL RETURNING id

typed_oracle.sql_law: DELETE WHERE amount IS NULL removes exactly the id=3 row and returns its id; explicit NULL is TRUE for IS NULL, not UNKNOWN.

cases.sql: DELETE FROM orders WHERE id = 1

typed_oracle.sql_law: DELETE id=1 removes one target row; NULL id and other keys remain unchanged. Cascade effects cannot be inferred without authoritative FK actions.

typed_oracle.sql_law: MERGE matched target id=1 updates from customer amount=100; two separate unmatched customer id=4 rows each insert (4,40), retaining bag multiplicity.

cases.sql: MERGE INTO orders o USING customers c ON o.id = c.id WHEN MATCHED AND c.amount > 0 THEN DELETE WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET amount = c.amount

typed_oracle.sql_law: Ordered MERGE WHEN branches select first matching positive source amount and DELETE target id=1; no later UPDATE branch can also execute.

cases.sql: MERGE INTO orders o USING customers c ON o.id = c.id WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (id) VALUES (c.id)

typed_oracle.sql_law: MERGE matched id=1 DELETE plus two unmatched customer id=4 INSERT(id) results in two distinct (4,NULL) target rows.

cases.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v AS SELECT id FROM orders

cases.sql: CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE tmp AS SELECT id FROM orders

cases.sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN amount INT

cases.sql: DROP TABLE orders

cases.sql: ALTER TABLE orders RENAME TO archived_orders

cases.sql: TRUNCATE TABLE orders

typed_oracle.sql_law: TRUNCATE clears the entire target physical bag but preserves the relation identity and schema.

cases.sql: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN amount SET DEFAULT 0
